solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Liqueur, like punch, over after a month

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the month, so it leads the answer

parts.note: MAR is the abbreviation for March
as means like
to chin someone is to punch them on the chin
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A drinker describes a liqueur as packing a punch, coming at the end of a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' is a verb here: to chin someone is to hit them on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sweet cherry liqueur from Dalmatia, made from marasca cherries.

clue.text: Draw out minutes and sort

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: Instructions to extend a session by some minutes and get things organised.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk something is to extract or exploit it to the full, drawing out every last bit.

clue.text: Hotelier slowing down by sharp double bend

parts.note: rit. is the musical abbreviation for ritardando, slowing down
the letter Z is shaped like a sharp double bend, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hotel owner slowing down for a tricky double bend on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: César Ritz was the Swiss hotelier who founded the Ritz hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: César Ritz founded the famous luxury hotels that still carry his surname.

clue.text: America's mischief, awfully sly, left UK bearing new grudge

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly arranged, so they are shuffled
new says the word grudge is itself given a fresh order before joining the rest

explanation.surface: A sly figure leaves Britain nursing a grudge, up to mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' warns that this is the American spelling, with SK rather than SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulduggery is underhand trickery; the double-L spelling is the American form of the word.

clue.text: Designed by boffins, possibly in white coats

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words white coats

explanation.surface: Scientists in white lab coats are the ones who design advanced gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffins are scientists in British slang; HI-TEC sits across 'wHITE Coats'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tec, high technology, describes sophisticated gear that scientists might devise.

clue.text: Some tack, based on changes, going in opposite directions

indicators.note: changes says the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: north and south are opposite compass directions, N and S

explanation.surface: A sailing tack that keeps changing, going first one way then the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' is not sailing but horse equipment; 'going in' simply joins the compass points to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is a rider's harness gear; a noseband is the strap of a bridle around a horse's nose.

clue.text: Send unsolicited plans back

indicators.note: back says the word for plans is read in reverse

parts.note: maps are plans, as in plans of an area

explanation.surface: An instruction to return some uninvited proposals.
explanation.definitionFit: To spam is to send unwanted bulk email messages to people who never asked for them.

clue.text: One receiving pay slip: ring line guaranteeing payment?

parts.note: a pro, professional, is paid for the work
a miss is a slip or failure
O is ring-shaped
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A paid worker is handed a slip ringing to confirm the money will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A promissory note is a written undertaking to pay a sum of money later.

clue.text: State graduate will bring in no money

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
read as 'is to gross': to gross is to bring in as earnings
O is nothing, zero, so no money

explanation.surface: A graduate's assurance that they will earn something, though nothing yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is the Brazilian state, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mato Grosso is a large state in western Brazil, its name meaning thick forest.

clue.text: Key indicator in case covering appeal: a necessity

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps around the others

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
it is sex appeal
a must is a necessity

explanation.surface: An advertiser's pitch for a key indicator in its case, calling it essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A litmus test is a decisive test, from the chemical indicator paper that shows acidity.

clue.text: Custom I'm not going to obey!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a refusal, 'I ...', which with the apostrophe dropped spells the same letters

explanation.walkthrough: The defiant shout is read as WON'T, the apostrophe ignored as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont as a noun means a habitual practice, while the contraction expresses a refusal to comply.

clue.text: Scan picture, and most of the sketch

parts.note: a flick is a film or moving picture

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the is lost

parts.note: a rough is a preliminary sketch

explanation.surface: Looking over a picture and the bulk of a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To flick through a book is to glance quickly over its pages, skimming the contents.

clue.text: Exclusion of chess player crying out to be heard

parts.note: Black is one of the two sides in chess

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: bawling is loud crying

explanation.surface: A chess player shut out of a club is loudly protesting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech bawling and balling sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackballing is voting against admitting someone to a club, so it means rejection or ostracism.

clue.text: Equal time needed by soldier, perhaps, on a horse

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the following pieces after the soldier

parts.note: a soldier ant is one kind of ant
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A cavalryman needs time equal to his mount's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier, perhaps' points to an insect, not a trooper: a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount to means equivalent in value or effect, as in 'tantamount to a confession'.

clue.text: Band — collective appearing in seedy venue?

parts.note: a strip is a band, a narrow piece
joint means shared or collective

explanation.surface: A band and its collective perform at a rough club.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip joint is a nightclub with striptease, often regarded as sleazy.

clue.text: The stuff of legend: from day one being seen in a sweater!

indicators.note: being seen in places these letters inside the jumper

parts.note: an Aran is a thick knitted jumper from the Aran Islands
THUR is short for Thursday
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a sweater on their first day becomes legendary.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian tales are the legends of King Arthur and the Round Table.

clue.text: Tax nicely adjusted? Not quite!

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A tax bill nicely adjusted is not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexactly means imprecisely, so 'not quite' describes something approximately but not precisely so.

clue.text: Superior catch, perhaps, one that is in firm grip?

indicators.note: in says the first letters go into the firm
grip says the firm holds the others inside

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
I is the Roman numeral one
sc., scilicet, is the Latin abbreviation for namely, that is

explanation.surface: A wrestler holds someone superior in a firm grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is Lake Superior, where this fish is caught; SC (scilicet) is less familiar than i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: The cisco is a freshwater whitefish of the Great Lakes, a fisherman's catch in Lake Superior.

clue.text: Object to having invite not guaranteed at first

indicators.note: at first says take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an invitation that comes with no guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb with 'to', but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object, any item or article.

clue.text: Eyes smart manoeuvres that carry a fair amount of interest?

definitions.text: that carry a fair amount of interest?

indicators.note: manoeuvres means these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Clever eyes moving toward something of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are hire-purchase instalments, and the interest charged on them is a fair-sized sum.

clue.text: Important double save: top class work, by George!

indicators.note: double says the word for save appears twice in a row

parts.note: major means important
bar means save, except, as in 'all bar one'
A is the top class or grade

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising an important double save as top-class work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'by George!' exclamation hides George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Major Barbara is a play by George Bernard Shaw, first staged in 1905.

clue.text: Call for House to scrap leave

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
go means leave

explanation.surface: A demand for the House to throw out a leave policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the bingo call, not Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of housey-housey, a winner shouts the game's name or 'House' on completing a card.

clue.text: Starts or finishes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: starts, as of races
second meaning: slang for kills, finishes off

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a plural noun for race starts and as a slang verb for killing someone.

clue.text: God reveals that bishop has departed

indicators.note: has departed means that letter is taken away

parts.note: bares means reveals
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: God shows that a bishop has left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war.

clue.text: For The Listener, the solvers join together as one

indicators.note: for the listener says the words are taken by sound; The Listener is also a crossword

parts.note: you, the solvers reading this; knit means join together

explanation.surface: Listener crossword solvers come together as one body.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one.

clue.text: Mean to keep winning, becoming champion

indicators.note: to keep says the outer phrase holds the next letters

parts.note: stand for means mean, signify
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A mean competitor who keeps winning becomes champion.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support and defend it.

clue.text: Scanty attire of old king showing his belly again?

parts.note: Tut is Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian king

indicators.note: his belly again means the centre letter of that name repeated

parts.note: his refers to the old king, giving the same name again

explanation.surface: An old king's skimpy costume shows his stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is a ballerina's short, stiff skirt.

clue.text: Jabber in front of MI6, providing possible explanation

indicators.note: in front of places the jabber first

parts.note: a hypo, hypodermic syringe, is a jabber
MI6 is the SIS, the Secret Intelligence Service, so the SIS

explanation.surface: A talker chatters in front of the spy agency, giving an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' suggests chatter but means something that jabs: a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation still to be tested.
